answers.question: Write your outline of the loop in the code block: what it remembers, what it repeats, and every way it stops.
answers.answer:
Remember: The message history (so far), what is the total lookup limit (12 in this case), and which number of lookup we are currently on (none yet)

while Claim is non empty:
    Call the model with the message history so far, and ask for its next step
    If the model has an answer:
        Reply with that answer
        Stop
    Else:
        If the lookup count is at the limit or one above the limit:
            Reply with "No Verdict"
            Stop
        For each lookup asked for
            Add 1 to the lookup count
        Once every lookup has its result add what they returned to the message history

answers.question: List each thing your loop remembers from one turn to the next, and say what would go wrong without it.
answers.answer: Each thing that my loop remembers from one turn to the next is the message history (so far), the total lookup limit (this case we are given 12), and the number we are currently on out of the lookup limit. Without the lookup limit then the model would just continously continue to run until it comes up with an answer but this would delay a reply and add complexity if we have alot of claims, so having a limit allows us to constrain the model. Additionally we must have message history incoporated so the model can troubleshoot what it already attempted and work from there, instead of starting from a blank canvas everytime to validate a claim.

answers.question: Now open `reference_loop.py` and compare it with your loop. Describe one difference in implementation and the resulting effects on agent behavior.
answers.answer: Comparing both loops I can see that they are kind of similiar in structure except the referene loop looks more concise. One difference in the implementation is that in my loop I put the logic of "for each lookup asked for (by the model)" in the else branch if the model has no answer, while the reference loop does not have the logic of whether or not the model asked for a lookup, it assumes it does, so the resulting effect on the agent is that it would loop over the reply.lookups even if there was not really any lookups asked for by the model.
